$comment: The approved-term register. Every rule is evidence-based: it was added because the drift it names was measured in this repository, not because it sounded like a rule. Each rule carries a positive control the checker asserts before it scans, so a dead regex cannot read as an all-clear.

rules.say: No postfix `live` modifier. Write "the node's live ring", or name what happened: "the halt the 0.2.9 deploy caused on testnet". Predicate and adverb uses are fine: "keeps the chain live", "follow the chain live", "chain liveness".
Marketing adjective. State the property instead: not "robust", but "tolerates one outlier component"; not "battle-tested", but "in production since <date>".

rules.pattern: \b(simply|note that|please note|it is worth noting|needless to say|at the end of the day|as you can see|of course,)\b
rules.control: Note that absent components simply drop out
rules.say: Filler. Delete it — the sentence says the same thing. "Note that X" is just "X".

rules.pattern: \b(worth (?:turning|having|its salt)|under the hood|out of the box|heavy lifting|secret sauce|the magic|a dial|moving parts|first and foremost|make no mistake)\b
rules.say: Mannered prose. Write the plain thing: "a parameter worth varying", "internally", "by default".

rules.control: in order to place an order
top up the orderbook on the test network
rules.say: Use the approved term: deposit / order book / cancel / testnet / sub-account / gateway. One term per concept — see STYLE.md.
No exclamation marks in a reference. A terminal reads flat.
Say what it actually has: "has its own balance, positions and orders". `concepts/sub-accounts.md` is exempt — it defines the term there and the definition is load-bearing.

Dead host. The public endpoint is `api.testnet.mtf.exchange`. `api.devnet` answers but its faucet reserve is empty and its books are one-sided; the two `*-gateway` aliases and `status.mtf.exchange` do not resolve at all. `docs/networks.md` is the one page allowed to name the dead endpoint, to say it is not the one to use.
